units.title: Scaffold packages/widgets (@fm/widgets) and add every native widget dependency to finance, notes, recipes + pnpm-lock
units.acceptance: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm turbo run lint typecheck test --filter=@fm/widgets
units.notes: STOP by gate-check (pnpm-lock.yaml). Brief 0004 Known gates. Do the whole lockfile change in this one unit so no later unit for finance, notes or recipes touches the lockfile. Add react-native-android-widget, @bacons/apple-targets (devDependency), expo-background-task and expo-task-manager, plus @fm/widgets workspace:* in each app. The shared Expo config plugin ships from packages/widgets/app.plugin.js (u06), NOT packages/config, so packages/config stays untouched. tsconfig and eslint extend @fm/config without editing it. Over 5 files because a lockfile change cannot be split.

units.title: @fm/widgets: widget declaration API, snapshot schema and the platform size map
units.acceptance: pnpm turbo run lint typecheck test --filter=@fm/widgets
units.notes: One declareWidgets() per app: id, kinds, sizes, deep-link route. Snapshot = versioned JSON with only displayed fields + state ok|error|signedOut + refreshedAt. Size map follows the brief's default: 4x1/4x2 map to medium, 2x2/2x1 to small, 4x3 to large, and a size the platform cannot render is dropped. Test the map and the snapshot round-trip.

units.title: @fm/widgets: native snapshot store (iOS App Group UserDefaults, Android SharedPreferences) + publishSnapshot()
units.acceptance: pnpm turbo run lint typecheck test --filter=@fm/widgets
units.notes: A local Expo module so no third-party storage dependency is needed. iOS writes to UserDefaults(suiteName: appGroup) and calls WidgetCenter.reloadAllTimelines(). Android writes to SharedPreferences and asks react-native-android-widget to re-render. The JS side only does TS checks. The Kotlin code is compiled by f04, n04 and r04 (release APK). The Swift code is compiled by check-ios-widgets on macOS. Depends on u02 because of the snapshot type and the shared index.ts.

units.title: @fm/widgets: headless session + widget action dispatcher (ok / error / 'Open app to sign in')
units.acceptance: pnpm turbo run lint typecheck test --filter=@fm/widgets
units.notes: Read path only on @fm/auth: build SessionManager over secureTokenStore and createClients from @fm/api outside React. Android headless JS runs in the app process, so no shared store is needed there. A refresh rejection or a missing session gives the signedOut state. A failed action gives the error state with no retry and no queue (non-goal). No edit under packages/auth. Blast radius: pkg:@fm/auth has 4 dependents, read only. Depends on u03 because it publishes the resulting snapshot and shares index.ts.

units.title: @fm/widgets: refresh scheduler (background task at most every 15 min) + refresh-after-mutation hook
units.acceptance: pnpm turbo run lint typecheck test --filter=@fm/widgets
units.notes: expo-background-task (WorkManager on Android, BGTaskScheduler on iOS), minimumInterval of 15 min. useRefreshWidgetsOnMutation(queryClient) subscribes to the TanStack mutation cache and republishes the snapshot after any successful write. iOS timeline policy .after(15 min) only re-reads the snapshot.

units.title: @fm/widgets: Expo config plugin (Android widget receivers, WidgetKit target wiring, App Group + keychain entitlements)
units.acceptance: pnpm turbo run lint typecheck test --filter=@fm/widgets
units.notes: Composes the react-native-android-widget, @bacons/apple-targets and expo-background-task plugins from one apps-facing entry: plugins: [['@fm/widgets', { widgets: [...] }]]. App Group = group.<ios.bundleIdentifier>, also used as the keychain access group. Expose it as expo.extra.widgets.appGroup (read by u08 and the Swift kit). The Apple team ID comes from process.env.FM_APPLE_TEAM_ID and is optional, so unsigned prebuild and compile work without it. Never commit a team ID. Swift colours are generated as asset-catalog colorsets from @fm/config/organic.preset.cjs, with no colour literals. Files are disjoint from u02-u05 (no index.ts), so it runs in parallel with them.

units.title: @fm/auth: on iOS store the session in the App Group keychain access group so the widget extension can read it
units.acceptance: pnpm turbo run lint typecheck test --filter=@fm/auth
units.notes: Human review is required by the brief's Known gates (security-sensitive token storage) even though packages/auth is not in the gate-check STOP column, so gate-check will NOT catch this one. Blast radius: pkg:@fm/auth has 4 dependents (finance, notes, recipes, @fm/api). Pass accessGroup = expo.extra.widgets.appGroup to expo-secure-store on iOS only, and migrate an existing item from the default group once. When the key is absent, behaviour must stay byte-for-byte as it is today. Android stays unchanged. No change to refresh logic, lifetimes or the state machine. The iOS extension only reads a non-expired access token and never refreshes, which avoids a refresh-rotation race that would revoke the token chain. Only the iOS App Intent units (f07, n07, t09) depend on this.

units.title: justfile: per-app build-apk-release/install-apk-release + check-ios-widgets recipe
units.acceptance: just build-apk-release emulator finance
units.notes: justfile is not in the STOP column. Signature build-apk-release env='production' app='recipes' (same as 0003 p8, so existing callers keep working; whichever brief lands first, the other's unit only needs its acceptance run). check-ios-widgets app: run expo prebuild -p ios --no-install --clean, assert the widget target is in the generated pbxproj, and on Darwin run pod install + xcodebuild CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO. Off Darwin it skips the compile with a message, except that it fails when CI=true (the same pattern as check-desktop).

units.title: BLOCKED QUESTION: the recipes basket has no server state. Where does a widget tick-off write?
units.acceptance: pnpm turbo run lint typecheck test --filter=@fm/app-recipes
units.notes: apps/recipes/components/basket.tsx holds the basket and its checked items in React useState only. It is not persisted, and recipes.v1 has no basket rpc (only SumIngredients and TotalIngredients). The brief's 'basket update' RPC does not exist. Human decision: (a) persist the basket on the device (snapshot store / AsyncStorage) and let the Android widget tick items locally, with iOS tap-to-open; (b) add a server-side basket to recipes.v1 + service:recipes, which goes beyond the brief's 'no new backend model' non-goal and is a new brief; or (c) drop the basket widget. The basket widget units (renderer, action, iOS target) will be added once this is answered.
